title: The wedding
logline: Saturday. The wedding. The strip draws it in the pavilion's glass: the ceremony as reflections, the Sound through it, the gown as light. Wood in the back row, the sketchbook closed on his lap for the only hour of the trip.

panels.composition: The glass pavilion from outside, afternoon: the ceremony visible through the glass, and the Sound reflected over it, so the guests sit in water. The gown a shape of light at the far end. Razor perspective.

characters.pose: a shape of light in the glass

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a glass and cedar pavilion seen from outside with a wedding visible through its glass overlaid by reflections of blue water so the seated guests appear to sit in the sound, a white gown as a shape of light at the far end, pristine architectural perspective, no words
image.notes: The ceremony only as reflection. Never a close face. The gown as light.

panels.composition: Inside: the back row. WOOD, the sketchbook closed on his lap. His hands on it. Not opening it. The only hour of the trip.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a thin man in a dark suit in the back row of a wedding with a closed sketchbook on his lap and both hands resting on it, no words

panels.composition: His hands on the closed cover. Ink on the fingers. Holding still.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, close-up of two ink-stained hands resting on a closed sketchbook cover, no words

panels.composition: The pavilion from outside again, later: the doors open, the guests spilling onto the lawn as color, the light going gold. The glass now reflecting only sky. Held.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a glass pavilion from outside with its doors thrown open and guests spilling onto a lawn as blurs of color in gold evening light, the glass reflecting only sky, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The ceremony as reflection. The sketchbook closed for one hour.
